UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user in the TrackFlow system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

role.description: User's role within the system (requester, approver, admin, safety, mm_team).

MaterialMovementRequest.title: MaterialMovementRequest
MaterialMovementRequest.description: Represents a request for material movement.

id.description: Unique identifier for the MaterialMovementRequest entity.

requesterId.description: Reference to UserProfile. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N MaterialMovementRequest) The user who created the request.

quantity.description: Quantity of the material being moved.

value.description: Value of the material in monetary units.

isReturnable.description: Indicates whether the material is returnable (true/false).

requiresDC.description: Indicates whether a Delivery Challan is required (true/false).

vehicleNumber.description: Vehicle number used for the movement (mandatory if value > ₹1,00,000).

ewayBillUrl.description: URL of the E-Way bill document.

status.description: Current status of the request (Pending, Approved, Rejected).

approvalIds.description: References to Approvals. (Relationship: Approval 1:N MaterialMovementRequest) List of approvals associated with the request.

ScrapMovementRequest.title: ScrapMovementRequest
ScrapMovementRequest.description: Represents a request for scrap material movement.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ScrapMovementRequest entity.

requesterId.description: Reference to UserProfile. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N ScrapMovementRequest) The user who created the request.

scrapType.description: Type of scrap material (Plastic, E-waste, Metal, etc.).

photoUrl.description: URL of the photo of the scrap material (for weight measurement).

approvalIds.description: References to Approvals. (Relationship: Approval 1:N ScrapMovementRequest) List of approvals associated with the request.

WorkPermitRequest.title: WorkPermitRequest
WorkPermitRequest.description: Represents a request for a work permit.

id.description: Unique identifier for the WorkPermitRequest entity.

requesterId.description: Reference to UserProfile. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N WorkPermitRequest) The user who created the request.

building.description: Building where the work will be performed (KOSMO, Test Tower).

activityType.description: Type of activity to be performed.

attachmentUrls.description: URLs of attachments (work orders, safety instructions).

approvalIds.description: References to Approvals. (Relationship: Approval 1:N WorkPermitRequest) List of approvals associated with the request.

id.description: Unique identifier for the DeliveryChallan entity.

materialMovementRequestId.description: Reference to MaterialMovementRequest. (Relationship: MaterialMovementRequest 1:1 DeliveryChallan) The associated material movement request.

materialList.description: List of materials being delivered (can be serialized string).

Approval.title: Approval
Approval.description: Represents an approval record for a request.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Approval entity.

approverId.description: Reference to UserProfile. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Approval) The user who performed the approval.

comment.description: Optional comment provided by the approver.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to ensure authorization independence, clarity, and scalability. User profiles are stored in `/userProfiles/{userProfileId}`. Material, Scrap, and Work Permit Requests are stored under `/users/{userId}/materialMovementRequests/{materialMovementRequestId}`, `/users/{userId}/scrapMovementRequests/{scrapMovementRequestId}`, and `/users/{userId}/workPermitRequests/{workPermitRequestId}` respectively to clearly establish ownership and allow easy querying of requests per user. Approvals are stored in a subcollection `approvals` within each request document, such as `/users/{userId}/materialMovementRequests/{materialMovementRequestId}/approvals/{approvalId}`. This structure supports the app requirements and enables simple and robust security rules that are easy to debug.

Authorization Independence:
Each request document (MaterialMovementRequest, ScrapMovementRequest, WorkPermitRequest) includes the `requesterId`, effectively denormalizing the user ID. This eliminates the need for `get()` calls to the `/users/{userId}` document to verify ownership, enabling atomic operations and simpler security rules. Similarly, for collaborative scenarios, if a request needs to be accessible by multiple users (e.g., approvers), relevant user roles or group memberships can be denormalized into the request document.

QAPs (Rules are not Filters):
The segregation of requests into user-specific subcollections enables secure `list` operations. Rules can easily enforce that a user can only list requests under their own user ID (`/users/{userId}/materialMovementRequests`). For admin or MM team access, a separate top-level collection (e.g., `/materialMovementRequests`) could be used, with denormalized access control information (e.g., `members: {uid: role}`) copied into each document to authorize listing based on role membership. This design avoids filtering based on document content, thus maintaining security and performance.
